_comment: Pterodactyl egg for Open Grind Web (og-server + SvelteKit build). Generated by server/pterodactyl/make-egg.py from bootstrap.sh; the install itself is server/pterodactyl/install.sh in the repository.
name: Open Grind Web
author: noreply@example.com
description: Self-hosted web backend for Open Grind: serves the app as a home-screen web app (iPhone) and talks to Grindr. Builds from your git repository at install (about 4 GB of free disk needed while building, ~30 MB after); Reinstall to update. Data in /home/container/data survives reinstalls.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Open Grind Web — the egg's installation script. Kept tiny on purpose: it
# clones the repository and runs server/pterodactyl/install.sh from it, so
# install fixes ship with a plain Reinstall instead of a new egg import.
# Works on the server's volume, not /tmp (a small tmpfs under Wings).
set -euo pipefail

export OG_BUILD=/mnt/server/.build
rm -rf "$OG_BUILD"
mkdir -p "$OG_BUILD/tmp"
export TMPDIR="$OG_BUILD/tmp"

apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates >/dev/null

echo "==> Source: ${GIT_URL} (${GIT_BRANCH})"
URL="${GIT_URL}"
if [ -n "${GIT_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
	# private repository: https://<token>@host/owner/repo.git
	URL="$(echo "${GIT_URL}" | sed -E "s#^https://#https://${GIT_TOKEN}@#")"
fi
git clone --quiet --depth 1 --branch "${GIT_BRANCH}" "${URL}" "$OG_BUILD/src"

exec bash "$OG_BUILD/src/server/pterodactyl/install.sh"

variables.name: Git repository
variables.description: HTTPS URL of your Open Grind Web repository (the fork with server/).

variables.name: Git token
variables.description: Access token for a private repository (leave empty for a public one).

variables.name: Password hash
variables.description: Optional argon2 hash of a gate password (og-server hash-password). Leave empty to use only authenticator codes.

variables.name: Authenticator secret
variables.description: Optional TOTP secret (base32). Leave empty: one is generated on first start and its QR code shown in the console.

variables.name: Trusted proxies
variables.description: Number of reverse proxies in front of the server (1 behind Caddy/Nginx Proxy Manager/Traefik, 0 if none). The proxy must be on this machine or a private network.
